main_text.head: CAPUT XXVII. DE PSYCHOLOGIA HUMANA, SEU ANIMA Hominis rationali.
main_text.p: Ἀνθρω-πολογία.ANthropologia est pars Zoographiæ, hominis naturam explicans.
Hominis natura est essentia spiritualis & corporeæ naturæ in unum ὑφιστάμενον [?] u-nitæ particeps.
Eius partes.Hominis partes sunt duæ: Anima logi-ca seu Spiritus humanus, & Corpus humanum.
Proinde Antropologiæ partes duæ sunt, Psychologia, & Somatotomia.
PSYCHOLOGIA est prior pars Anthropologiæ, quæ docet naturam animæ seu spiritus humani per ejusdem fa-cultates.ψυχο-λογία.

Est autem Anima rationalis pars hominis essentialis, nimirum Spiritus humano corpori animando destinatus, eiq; in unam hypostasin unitꝰ [?], suis facultatibus actiones in illo vel per illud ciens.Anima rationalis.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek word after "in unum" is read as ὑφιστάμενον and is uncertain. The word after "in unam hypostasin" is read as unitꝰ, but it may be unitæ; it is marked [?]. The Greek catchwords in the left margin are hyphenated across two lines. The faint "Caput" at the bottom left is show-through and is left out. The first paragraph's large initial A is joined to "Nthropologia" as ANthropologia.
